title: Outcome
description:
One triaged alert: what was judged, what was decided, and what was
written back.

See `docs/triage.md`, section "The outcome contract", for the shape rules
and the evolution policy.

alert.description: The alert as the model saw it.

component.description:
The alerting component in the software catalog; `null` when Backstage
is not configured or nothing matched.

decided_at.description: When the decision was reached, RFC 3339.

impact.description:
The impact level the policy used. Always equals
`judgments.impact.level`; repeated at the top level because it is
half of the routing decision.

incident.description:
The incident to attach to; `null` unless the decision is
`attach_to_incident`. It names the target even in a dry run:
`writes.attached` says whether the attachment happened.

model.description:
The versioned model that answered, e.g. `jev-1.13.0`. Thresholds are
tuned per version.

owner.description:
The team the decision addresses; `null` for `suppress` and
`attach_to_incident`.

recent_changes.description: Recent changes offered to the model as possible causes.

related_alerts.description: Other alerts firing in the window, newest first.

runbook_url.description: The runbook page the alert was read against.

signalman_version.description: The signalman build that produced the document.

suspected_change.description:
Whether a listed recent change is flagged as the likely cause. Only
ever true for `page` and `ticket`.

tags.description:
The `ai-*` tags written on the alert, or that would be written. Every
one is derivable from the fields above.

time_to_qualify_seconds.description:
Seconds from the alert's creation to the decision. `null` when the
alert carries no creation time, as on the file-based CLI.

windows.description: How far back the two lookups reached.

Action.description:
What signalman decided to do with the alert. The vocabulary of the
`decision` field and of the `ai-action-*` tag (which is hyphenated:
`human_triage` is tagged `ai-action-human-triage`, and
`attach_to_incident` is tagged `ai-action-attach`).

oneOf.description: Nobody needs to act; log and drop.
The same underlying problem as an incident that is already open.
Wake the owning team now.
Open a ticket for the owning team; no page.
A person decides: the owner is not clear enough to route.

AlertRef.description: The alert as the model saw it.

created_at.description:
When the alert was created, RFC 3339. `null` when the source does not
say.

id.description: incident.io alert id (a ULID). `null` when the alert came from a file.

labels.description: The labels the model saw, after merging the alert's own tags.

source.description:
Emitting system, exactly as it was sent in the state: `prometheus`, or
`incident.io alert source <id>` on the webhook path.

source_url.description: Link back to the monitor or query that fired.

ChangeRef.description:
A deploy, configuration change or feature flag offered to the model as a
possible cause. Everything but `summary` is `null` when the alert carried
its changes as plain lines instead of through the change feed.

component.description: The component it touched; `null` means platform-wide.

summary.description: One line: what changed, which version, who did it.

url.description: Link to the deploy, merge request or commit.

ComponentRef.description: The alerting component as the software catalog knows it.

catalog_owner.description:
The owner the catalog records, as a display name. Not the same thing
as `owner`: this is what the catalog says, `owner` is what signalman
decided.

dependents.description: What depends on it, as `kind name` strings: the blast radius.

depends_on.description: What it depends on, as `kind name` strings.

url.description: The component's page in the Backstage catalog.

DuplicateJudgment.description:
Whether the alert duplicates an open incident. The whole object is `null`
when the question was not asked because no incident was open.

candidates.description:
Every incident offered, most probable first. Excludes the "none"
option, whose probability is `none_probability`.

chosen.description:
The incident reference the model chose, or `null` when it chose the
"new, separate problem" option.

confidence.description:
How concentrated the distribution is. Compared against
`policy.attach_confidence`.

none_probability.description: Probability the alert is a new, separate problem.

Forwarded.description: The alert the CLI forwarded to an incident.io HTTP alert source.

deduplication_key.description: The key incident.io deduplicated the event under.

ImpactJudgment.description: How bad it is for users.

distribution.description: Probability of every level, always four rows, lowest level first.

level.description:
The level nearest to `score`. This is what the policy compares
against `policy.page_at`, and what the top-level `impact` repeats.

score.description:
Probability-weighted position on the scale, `0.0..=3.0`. It may fall
between levels: 2.6 is "worse than major, not quite an outage".

ImpactLevel.description:
User-facing impact, lowest first. The same vocabulary as the
`ai-impact-*` tag and as `policy.page_at`.

oneOf.description: Internal, informational, or non-production only.
A small subset of users, or one non-critical feature, degraded.
Most users degraded, or a critical feature unavailable.
The product is unavailable, or data integrity is at risk, for everyone.

ImpactOption.description: One level of the impact scale with its probability.

probability.description: Probability the impact is at this level.

IncidentOption.description: One open incident offered as a duplicate candidate.

id.description: incident.io incident id (a ULID), when it was fetched from the API.

probability.description: Probability this alert is the same underlying problem.

url.description: The incident in the incident.io app.

IncidentRef.description:
An incident this alert belongs to. Its dedup confidence is not repeated
here: it is `judgments.duplicate_of.confidence`.

id.description: incident.io incident id (a ULID), when it was fetched from the API.

url.description: The incident in the incident.io app.

Judgments.description: Everything the model judged. One question, one field.

actionable.description: Probability a person must act now rather than let it resolve itself.

caused_by_change.description:
Probability a listed recent change caused it; `null` when no change
was listed, so the question was never asked.

duplicate_of.description:
Whether it duplicates an open incident; `null` when no incident was
open, so the question was never asked.

impact.description: How bad it is for users.

owner.description: Who should own the first response.

NoteStatus.description: What became of the qualification note.

oneOf.description: A new note was created on the alert.
The note signalman left on an earlier pass was rewritten in place.
Writing the note failed; `error` says why. The tags were still written.
The note is switched off in the configuration.
No note was attempted: a dry run, or the detached CLI.

NoteWrite.description: The qualification note signalman writes on the incident.io alert.

id.description: The note's id when one was written.

OwnerJudgment.description: Who should own the first response.

chosen.description: The option the model chose. May be `none_of_these`.

confidence.description:
How concentrated the distribution is. Not the probability of
`chosen`: that is in `options`.

options.description: Every option offered, including `none_of_these`, most probable first.

OwnerOption.description: One option of the owner question, with the probability the model gave it.

entity_ref.description: Software-catalog reference, when the candidate came from Backstage.

key.description: Candidate key. `none_of_these` is the no-match option, always offered.

probability.description: Probability this is the owning team.

url.description: The team's page in the Backstage catalog.

OwnerRef.description:
The team the decision addresses. `null` unless the decision routes to
somebody (`page`, `ticket`, `human_triage`).

entity_ref.description:
Software-catalog reference (`group:default/payments`) when the
candidate came from Backstage; `null` for the built-in team list.

key.description: Candidate key, also the suffix of the `ai-team-*` tag.

status.description: How firmly the team is attributed.

url.description: The team's page in the Backstage catalog.

OwnerStatus.description: How firmly the owner is attributed.

oneOf.description: Routed to this team; owner confidence cleared the automatic threshold.

Routed to this team, but the responder should confirm ownership:
confidence was middling.

Nobody was confident enough to route; this is the best guess offered
to whoever triages by hand.

PolicySnapshot.description:
The thresholds in force when the decision was made. Kept in the document
because a decision is only interpretable against the policy that produced
it.

attach_confidence.description: Minimum dedup confidence to attach to an existing incident.

auto_route_confidence.description: Owner confidence at or above which routing is automatic.

flag_change_above.description: `caused_by_change` probability above which the change is flagged.

human_below_confidence.description: Owner confidence below which a person triages instead.

page_at.description: Impact at or above which the owner is paged rather than ticketed.

suppress_below.description: Below this `actionable` probability the alert is suppressed.

Probability.description:
One probability, as its own object so the field reads the same wherever
a yes/no judgment appears.

RelatedAlertRef.description:
Another alert firing in the same window: the blast radius as the alert
hub saw it when the decision was made.

component.description: The component it names, when it names one.

Usage.description: Token accounting for the one TypeSafe request behind this decision.

input_tokens.description: Tokens in the state plus all questions. These are the billed ones.

Windows.description:
How far back the two lookups reached. `null` means the lookup was not
performed at all.

change_seconds.description: Seconds of history searched in the change feed.

related_seconds.description: Seconds of history searched for other firing alerts.

WriteMode.description: Whether the side effects the document describes actually happened.

oneOf.description: Tags, attachment, note and notification were written back.
Everything was computed, nothing was written (evaluation runs).
The file-based CLI: there is no incident.io alert to write back to.

Writes.description: What signalman actually did, as opposed to what it decided.

attached.description: Whether the alert was attached to `incident`.

forwarded.description:
The forwarded alert event, when the CLI ran with
`--forward-to-incidentio`.

mode.description: Whether the side effects happened at all.

note.description: What became of the qualification note.

notified.description:
Catalog reference of the group notified through Backstage, when one
was notified.

tags_applied.description: Whether `tags` were written on the alert.
